title: service-automation: a connector credential written through the door reaches only the replica that took it; a held instance on any other replica stays down until a metadata reload or a restart
body:
domain:server#3 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXc5hequf76uJfzrdK
Filing gate: ② a reproducible behaviour defect found by the contract review of PR #27344 (record `6489576275`, ③ should-fix, "carrier owed"). Filed by `domain:server` seat 3 (`session_01Utp6CXc5hequf76uJfzrdK`). ⛔ Not a claim; left for triage.

## Defect

PR #27344 (#27237) adds the connector credential door: `PUT|DELETE /api/v1/automation/connectors/credential-refs/:ref` writes `sys_connector_credential` and reconciles the declarative connector instances naming the ref — **on the replica that took the request**. The os-dev report and the PR's acceptance say other replicas "pick it up on their next reconcile (degraded retry timer, metadata reload) or at restart". On the tree that is true only for an instance on the backoff:

- An instance whose STORED value its upstream refused is `held` (`holdConnectorForRejectedCredential`: `held = credential === undefined || stored !== undefined`) and is excluded from `scheduleDeclarativeRetry` — it has no timer.
- The re-`PUT` bumps the row's `revision`, but a held replica recomputes its reconcile signature (`credential:<fingerprint>` with `object:<revision>`) only on `metadata:reloaded` or at restart.

So on a multi-replica hosted environment — the case #27237 exists for — an administrator's corrected credential takes effect on one replica at once and on the others only after a publish or a restart. Requests landing on those replicas keep failing against a degraded instance.

## Ask

Propagate a credential write cluster-wide: a reload signal on the row change, or a short poll of the row's `revision` by held instances (and by `missing` ones, for symmetry). Pin it with a two-engine test sharing one store: a `PUT` on A re-materializes the held instance on B without a reload.

## Filing facts

- reach: every multi-replica deployment using the credential door; single-process deployments are unaffected (the card's acceptance holds there).
- Dedupe: #27237 / PR #27344 (the door itself; this is its out_of_scope_findings 1, understated). No open card on cross-replica credential propagation.
